transcript:
Meeting header:
Date/Time: 2025-12-19 15:00 UTC (54 minutes)
Location: Zoom
Recorded by: Fireflies
Attendees (as captured): Asha Patel, Marco Liu, Jonah Reyes — Redwood; Lena Ortiz, Dr. Samuel Reed, Maya Chen, Omar N'Diaye, Priya Malhotra — Bluewave Health

Summary (auto): Procurement intake to review MSA/DPA exception requests and SLA requirements for low-latency inference.

[00:00] Asha Patel (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick roll call then we'll jump in. I'm Asha, AE on the account, with Marco our SE and Jonah on pricing.
[00:12] Lena Ortiz (Customer - Procurement): Hi all, Lena here. We'll probably run through a handful of legal items and then hand to Samuel for the technical asks.
[00:18] Dr. Samuel Reed (Customer - CTO): Samuel here. Looking forward to understanding the SLA and the private deployment options.
[00:25] Maya Chen (Customer - Legal): Maya, legal. We'll be focused on MSA redlines and DPA specifics.
[00:29] Marco Liu (Redwood SE): Marco, thanks. I'll cover the network/KMS bits and how our private offering works.
[00:34] Jonah Reyes (Redwood CSM): Jonah, I'll jump in on pricing and committed capacity forecasts.
[00:39] Omar N'Diaye (Customer - InfoSec): Omar — short security questions from my side.
[00:44] Priya Malhotra (Customer - AI Platform): Priya — I'll ask about throughput and model roster.

[01:05] Asha: Okay, agenda: quick procurement path (who signs what), MSA/DPA exceptions, SLA targets for the EU inference workload, and pricing path. Anything to add?
[01:12] Lena: That covers it. We want to know who needs to approve pricing and where legal sits for the MSA redlines.

[02:10] Maya: To start, on the DPA — Bluewave is pushing for explicit data residency commitments for EU patient data and a tighter deletion window, 14 days after request. Also, we need clarity on subprocessors and a right to audit clause.
[02:25] Asha: Understood. Our standard DPA currently allows processing in specified regions and 30-day deletion by default; we can propose language to tighten to 14 days for EU PHI, though that will have operational implications if it's cross-region.
[02:40] Marco: Just to add, for private deployments (VPC) we can keep the data fully in-custody, which makes deletion semantics more straightforward. For hosted, we have to coordinate KV cache purges and blob lifecycle rules.
[02:55] Omar: What about key management — KMS versus HSM — do you support customer-managed keys in the private offering? We need HSM-backed keys for certain workloads.
[03:10] Marco: Yes, we support KMS integrations and customer-managed keys; HSM-backed KMS is supported in private installs. There's a short note in our compliance pack; I'll attach diagrams.

[04:00] Priya: For the inference SLA we need p95 latency under 150ms for short text completions and 1s for longer multimodal requests. Can Redwood commit to p95 at those numbers in eu-west?
[04:12] Jonah: Can I clarify, Priya, are those numbers for peak sustained throughput or for light load?
[04:18] Priya: Sustained, at about 200 qps for small models and 50 qps for larger models.
[04:26] Marco: Those are tight but plausible on dedicated pools. Hosted offering will be more variable; we generally target p95 under 200-300ms for small models but that is region and load dependent. For EU-specific SLAs we can propose a dedicated cluster with reserved capacity.
[04:40] Samuel: Cost will be a big factor. We need a delta for committed capacity vs burst.

[05:10] Asha: On the procurement side, who's the primary approver for contract exceptions on your end?
[05:16] Lena: Legal (Maya) + Procurement sign-off (me) for pricing thresholds above $200k ARR; lower than that we can auto-approve via procurement.
[05:24] Maya: And finance will look at the SLA credits — we don't want to see large credits that create weird incentives.

[06:05] Jonah: I'll put together a pricing packet showing 3 tiers: self-serve hosted trial, committed dedicated (monthly commit), and private VPC/on-prem. I'll include a committed throughput example and show per-token and per-embedding numbers with an example 12-month commit.
[06:20] Marco: For the SLA language, we have template phrasing: uptime % and latency p95 by model family and region. We can propose 99.9% monthly availability for dedicated clusters and include credits up to a cap. If you need custom remedies, that becomes an enterprise SLA negotiation.

[08:00] Maya: We have one exception request on the MSA — indemnity cap related to PHI processing. They want higher than our standard commercial cap. Is that something Redwood can flex on?
[08:12] Asha: We generally have a commercial cap; for regulated customers with PHI we consider carve-outs but need an internal legal review. I'll flag this as part of the redline package.
[08:22] Maya: Also, termination for convenience — they want a 90-day exit period with data return and assisted export.
[08:29] Marco: Assisted export is doable; we have export tooling and a one-time extraction service. For deletion we will document steps and timing.

[10:05] (inaudible) Speaker: ...
[10:20] Samuel: One more technical piece — model version pinning during rollouts. If we do canary deploys, will the KV cache behave correctly, or will we see cold starts?
[10:30] Marco: Good question. Our runtime supports sticky routing per-traffic slice; canary routes can be pinned to dedicated nodes which preserve KV cache. There is a small risk of cold-cache on first flip, but we've built in prefix caching to mitigate it. (transcription: K-V cash spelled 'kay vee cache' sometimes)
[10:48] Samuel: Good. That addresses reliability concerns.

[12:00] Lena: On the procurement timeline — we are aiming to finalize vendor approvals by mid-January. That means we need pricing and redlines before the procurement committee on 2026-01-09.
[12:12] Asha: We'll target sending everything by 2025-12-23 so you have time.

[15:14] Maya: About subprocessors — can Redwood provide a subprocessor list and commit to notice windows for new ones?
[15:22] Marco: Yes, we maintain a subprocessor page; for Dedicated/Private clients we can limit subprocessors to those within the region or to those we control. We'll include a notice window in the redline.

[18:05] Omar: Security: network diagrams, SOC 2 Type II, ISO 27001 if available, pen test reports. Also, can you support SAML SSO + SCIM provisioning for accounts?
[18:18] Marco: We support SAML SSO and SCIM for user provisioning; SOC 2 attestation is available and we have ISO readiness materials. We'll put all artifacts in the compliance folder link (link shared: https://redwood.internal/asset-pack/BWH-compliance).

[21:00] Priya: A practical ask — do you support synthetic load benchmarks or a joint-run benchmark so we can validate latency at our payload distribution?
[21:10] Marco: Yes, we do a joint benchmark. For dedicated pools we can run a workload mirror; we'll need an agreed dataset and time window. That can be part of the POC/Pilot scope.

[24:30] Jonah: Quick pricing questions — do you have any committed term discounts for 12 vs 24 months?
[24:36] Asha: Yes, we usually layer discounts by commit and term; Jonah will show typical tiers.

[28:00] Maya: For the DPA deletion window — 14 days is our preferred. If Redwood can meet that for EU PHI, that would materially reduce legal pushback.
[28:12] Marco: I'll note operational caveats: if data is replicated cross-region for resilience there are coordination steps, but for Private/VPC we can target 14-day service-level deletion.

[32:00] (brief cross talk)
[33:15] Asha: Let's recap actions: 1) Redwood sends redlined MSA/DPA; 2) Marco attaches compliance artifacts and network/KMS diagram; 3) Jonah sends pricing spreadsheet with committed vs burst; 4) customer to send their list of required exceptions.
[33:37] Lena: Correct — and procurement will run the pricing by finance by 2025-12-28.

[36:00] Maya: One nuance — on SLA credits we want recoverable service credits rather than cash; finance prefers credits applied to future invoices. Is that acceptable?
[36:12] Jonah: We often structure credits as service credits; we'll put that into the SLA template.

[40:05] Samuel: Two more technical items: 1) encryption in transit and at rest specifics (cipher suites), 2) telemetry retention for logs — what is the default retention and can we shorten?
[40:18] Marco: In transit uses TLS1.3 with modern ciphers; at rest we use AES-256. Telemetry retention by default is 90 days; for private you can request adjustments and we can discuss retention controls.

[44:00] Priya: If we go with private, what's the onboarding time? We have a hard deadline in late Feb for a soft launch.
[44:12] Asha: Private deployment onboarding typically runs 6–8 weeks from contract signature depending on hardware and network approvals. If you sign in early Jan we can aim for late Feb; need to sync with ops.

[48:22] Maya: For legal triage, we'll bring redlines and focus on indemnity, deletion SLA, subprocessors and audit rights.
[48:30] Asha: Sounds good. I'll propose a legal-only slot next week (see next steps).

[51:00] Lena: Any blockers from Redwood's side?
[51:06] Marco: Nothing blocking — just internal legal review for indemnity cap and we'll surface options in the redline.
[51:12] Jonah: Pricing piece is straightforward; we may need to iterate based on committed throughput.

[53:00] Asha: Great, thanks everyone. We'll send the artifacts and propose the legal triage meeting. Happy holidays early.
[53:09] All: Thanks, bye.
